correctness.rationale: The uniform weak-composition count gives p_j=binom(N-j+m-2,m-2)/binom(N+m-1,m-1); conditioning Y_2=b yields q_a(N-b). Hence for distinct a,b positive, Cov=m(m-1)p_b[q_a(N-b)-m p_a/(m-1)] with strictly positive p_b. Exact ratio q_a(L+1)/q_a(L) has numerator-minus-denominator a(m-2)-L-1 for L>=a, so q is unimodal (zero for L<a), and any strictly positive superlevel set is a single integer interval, even if the excluded b=a point interrupts actual cross-covariances. Independent exact fractions for m=4,N=12,a=2,b=7..10 reproduce (-48/29575,+108/41405,+72/41405,-876/207025); independent integer interval checks m=3..7,N=2..24. Formula is all finite m>=3, N>=2; no diagonal and no vacuum covariance claim.
residual_risks: Endpoint cases a+b>N are handled by q=0; finite checked ranges not general proof.

value.rationale: The sign of covariance between distinct occupancy frequency counts is a natural dependence statistic for uniform integer compositions. While the raw moment formula is elementary and known, the complete all-parameter one-island rule and strict negative-positive-negative witness supply an exact previously unrecorded qualitative classification; the missing diagonal is carefully distinguished. A future researcher could use this specific sign structure in occupancy inference rather than rederive multiple moment inequalities.
